source.title: Symmetric Divergence and Normalized Similarity: A Unified Topological Framework for Representation Analysis

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity with topological rank-based measures and compares them with geometric measures; it does not test convergence as model scale or capability increases.
record.gate_note: The study reports similarity analyses across TinyCNNs trained with different seeds and across LLM families, plus comparisons between metrics and a normalization ablation. Autoencoder quality results, runtime results, and cited findings are not rows because they do not measure representation alignment relevant to the claim. Heatmap results without a textual description are recorded as figure-only where relevant.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper: it proposes topological similarity measures (NTS, SRTD) and compares them with CKA, RSA and RTD on cross-model representations. Two of its results bear on the claim. Ten different-seed TinyCNNs are compared layer by layer across 45 pairs (a weak test of V3). The same 17 LLMs give different similarity patterns under CKA versus NTS-E, and with versus without Z-score normalization (V6). It does not test scale, capability or cross-modal convergence. Much of the paper is its own method's performance (autoencoder loss, runtime, synthetic clusters), which is not a test of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that NTS gives a bounded, scale-robust topological similarity that complements CKA, and that SRTD and SRTD-lite give fine-grained diagnostics and an efficient loss. They also say NTS recovers LLM family structure and distillation lineage where CKA saturates or drops. They frame the metric differences as NTS being better, not as evidence against convergence.
record.recipe_differences: Uses topological merge-order rank correlation (NTS) and cross-barcode divergence measures, with CKA and RSA comparisons. It does not reproduce a scale-and-capability experiment from the claim's original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with similarity measure (NTS versus CKA and SRTD-lite), dataset (TruthfulQA versus ToxiGen), and NTS Z-score normalization. The paper also presents LLM heatmaps at different layers, but does not describe those layer-specific results in text.

fits_no_version.finding: NTS shows consistent intra-model layer-similarity 'fingerprints' within LLM families (Qwen, InternLM, Baichuan, Llama) on TruthfulQA and ToxiGen. CKA does so only for InternLM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models sharing a lineage keep similar within-model layer-similarity structure across post-training, as detected by topological measures.

record.problems: The TinyCNN alignment results are aggregate layerwise heatmaps rather than direct feature or subspace comparisons. Most relevant heatmap values are not stated numerically in the text, and the LLM analysis focuses on selected datasets and layers. The study does not test convergence with increasing model scale or capability.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep. LLMs are compared only by family and lineage.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison.
Only layer-level similarity heatmaps are reported. Shared features or subspaces are not identified, and units or bases are not shown to differ.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation experiment.
No analysis of interpretable features or circuits.
The number of neighbours and out-of-distribution inputs are not varied for cross-model alignment. Effects of layer choice in LLMs are shown only as undescribed heatmaps.
There is no test of plateau or of the causes of alignment, though lineage is used as ground truth.

missing.what: Topological measures (NTS, SRTD-lite) show a sharp structural break at the final pooling layer across seed pairs that CKA and RSA miss. This is a metric-dependent cross-seed result.
The percentages in the Figure 6 captions (CKA 98.89%, NTS-E 97.22%, NTS-M 94.72%, SRTD-lite 98.33%) are not explained in the text and are not recorded as rows.
SRTD-lite and RTD-lite inter-LLM divergence scores at layers 6 and 12. These are dominated by single ultra-long barcodes, so the cross-model divergence depends on a few outlier pairs.

record.verdict_notes: This is mainly a methods paper. Its bearing on the claim is indirect: CKA versus NTS differences are presented to argue for NTS, but they show that measured cross-model similarity depends on the measure and on preprocessing. Nearly all evidence is figure-only with no numbers in the text, except CKA above 0.8. The within-model LLM rows were unlinked because they do not compare independently trained models' representations.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no test of independently trained models across architectures, objectives, data, or modalities as scale increases.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language representation comparison.
The study compares layerwise representations across different-seed TinyCNNs, but does not identify shared individual features, units, or subspaces, nor test whether bases or units differ.
No representation mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired mapping experiment.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
The study compares metrics, datasets, and Z-score normalization, but does not vary nearest-neighbour count or systematically test out-of-distribution inputs.
The study does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives causally explain it.

relationships.condition: Ten 8-layer TinyCNNs trained on CIFAR-10 from different seeds, averaged over 45 pairs
relationships.reason: CKA, NTS-E and NTS-M show corresponding layers most similar across seeds, decaying smoothly with depth distance. The evidence is at layer level only and figure-only (r1, r2, r3).
relationships.display_finding: CKA, NTS-E and NTS-M placed corresponding layers closest across seeds, with similarity declining smoothly as layer separation increased.

relationships.condition: 17 LLMs, TruthfulQA, layer 6: CKA versus NTS-E, and NTS-E with versus without Z-score normalization
relationships.reason: Inter-model similarity changes with the measure and its settings. CKA saturates above 0.8 while NTS-E spreads; the distilled pair is low under CKA but high under NTS-E; scores drop without normalization (r9–r13).
relationships.display_finding: CKA saturated above 0.8 while NTS-E spread scores, the distilled pair scored low under CKA but high under NTS-E, and removing normalization lowered scores.

relationships.condition: TinyCNN cross-seed layer comparisons under SRTD-lite versus normalized measures
relationships.reason: SRTD-lite gives irregular inversions where CKA, NTS and RSA give a smooth diagonal, so the measured cross-seed structure depends on the measure (r4). In this setting the normalized measures themselves agree.
relationships.display_finding: SRTD-lite produced irregular inversions, whereas CKA, NTS and RSA agreed on a smooth diagonal across cross-seed layer comparisons.
